plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, a behavior called heliotropism. It is widely cultivated for seed, oil, and ornamental use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, Argentina, and China
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not a single flower but a composite of up to 2,000 tiny florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower that forms dense, arching plumes of tiny golden flower heads at the top of its stems. It is a major late-summer nectar source for bees, butterflies, and other pollinators, and it thrives in meadows, roadsides, and open fields.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often wrongly blamed for hay fever; the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time but has wind-borne pollen.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like, goblet-shaped flowers in late summer or early autumn, long after its leaves have died back. The flowers emerge directly from the ground without foliage, earning it the nickname 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (late August to October)
plants.location: Native to meadows and woodlands of Europe; grown in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that is also used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant, golden ball-shaped flower clusters. In the Southern Hemisphere it blooms as winter turns to spring, brightening the bushland and gardens of southeastern Australia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July to October) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring in Australia.
